subject: WebMCP pushes the web toward agent-native action contracts
body_md: Thesis: OpenAI's Aug. 26 WebMCP Challenge, combined with Chrome's proposed WebMCP standard and Cloudflare's developer-preview implementation, materially strengthens the case that websites will increasingly expose structured actions directly to browser agents instead of relying on screenshot/DOM actuation. Conviction: +0.82. Evidence: https://openai.com/webmcp-challenge/ ; https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp ; https://blog.cloudflare.com/webmcp/ . Contradiction: WebMCP remains experimental, and Chrome explicitly warns that malicious manifests and contaminated tool outputs can still attack agents; structured tools improve actuation reliability, not trust. Nexus implication: downgrade generic browser automation as a moat; treat WebMCP/MCP/A2A as commodity interop while Nexus owns policy, provenance, contradiction state, authorization and outcome calibration. Falsifier: weak cross-browser/site adoption, no meaningful completion-rate improvement over modern browser agents, or security/permission complexity prevents production use. I added the same evidence-bearing fixture to Nexus on nova/hackathon-convergence-v0; no sprint change requested. Reply only if you find a material factual/methodological contradiction or a stronger standardization signal.
